title: Capacity playbook: latency-first ramp & allocations (NA/EU/APAC, 24mo)
content:
Context:
This is a working playbook for a latency-prioritized activation ramp across NA / EU / APAC over the next 24 months. Purpose is to capture a pragmatic allocation strategy that keeps p95/p99 latency SLOs stable while we onboard new GPU waves and allow regional demand to grow.

High-level goal:
- Keep p95 < 120ms for small-gen requests and p99 < 600ms for long-context generative workloads in each region during ramp windows.
- Limit sudden utilization spikes: target steady-state utilization band 45-68% per zone for first 6 months after activation.
- Provide deterministic fallback and model-variant routing when capacity is constrained.

Design constraints / assumptions (quick):
- Model mix baseline: 60% medium-generation (8k), 30% short-gen (2k), 10% embeddings and rerank.
- GPU types: N1 (dense 80GB), N2 (quantized 40GB) available per region; treat N2 as burst-only for latency-sensitive traffic until warmed.
- Burst reserve: 18% of total capacity pinned as hot reserve for p99 incidents.
- Network egress limits: EU region has 6% higher cross-az latency variance; APAC has spotty vendor availability in some zones.

Ramp cadence (phases):
- Phase 0 (pre-warm, 0-4 weeks): light synthetic load + canary traffic to validate kernel profiles, autoscaler configs, KV cache warmups.
- Phase 1 (controlled ramp, 4-12 weeks): bring utilization to 30-50%, enable model routing policy latency-first, begin regional traffic shaping.
- Phase 2 (throughput rollup, 3-9 months): increase to target steady-state utilization band, expand burst windows, open to more tenants.
- Phase 3 (saturation tests and handoff, 9-24 months): run long-duration soak tests, tune compaction/quantization, consider rebalancing between regions.

Trigger conditions for next tranche: (all must be green)
- p95 latency within 15% of baseline for 7 consecutive days in region.
- Error rates < 0.3% for HTTP 5xx and inference timeouts.
- KV cache hit ratio > 22% for frequent prefixes (or fallback plan in place).
- Autoscaler cooldowns behaved: no more than 2 emergency scale-ups per week.

Allocation table (simplified projection) - text table because Drive: 
Month | NA GPUs | EU GPUs | APAC GPUs | expected util % | p99 target (ms)
------|--------:|-------:|---------:|---------------:|-------------:
M0-1  | 120     | 60     | 30      | 10-25          | 400
M2-3  | 240     | 120    | 60      | 28-45          | 350
M4-6  | 420     | 200    | 110     | 40-58          | 300
M7-12 | 600     | 320    | 180     | 50-68          | 250
M13-24| 760     | 420    | 260     | 55-72          | 220

Notes on table: counts are logical GPU-equivalents (N1 baseline). We schedule GPUs in waves of 40 for NA, 20 for EU, 10-15 for APAC to keep provisioning atomic and predictable. The p99 numbers assume KV caching and small-model fallbacks available.

Latency-weighted routing policy (sketch):
- Route requests by region priority then latency budget: if p95 estimate for local pool + net < target, route local.
- If local predicted p95 shows degradation > 20% then route to nearest compatible fallback region with explicit cost multiplier tag.
- Add sticky routing for 60s to improve cache locality for short sessions.

Operational playbook (incident & scale):
- Monitoring: dashboards for GPU util, p50/p95/p99, KV hit ratio, autoscale events, queue depth per shard. Add synthetic user journeys every 5 minutes (short-gen + long-gen).
- Early-warning: if p95 drifts > 10% for 1h, open INCIDENT-P1 channel; run quick reroute to N2-quantized pool for best-effort degradation.
- Emergency fallbacks: redirect 20% of traffic to smaller models (fast-mode) and enable response streaming where possible.
- Postmortem knobs: Verify kernel selection logs, batching histograms, and cache warmup timing.

Cost / utilization optimization notes:
- Keep initial allocation conservative in APAC given vendor onboarding risk; plan for 10% rebalancing monthly if utilization delta between regions > 12%.
- Implement per-tenant soft caps during ramp to protect p99 SLOs for core customers.
- Run a monthly quantization candidate pass: identify models with less than 8% quality delta to move to N2 path.

Runbook checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm wave booking with cloud vendors (NA wave #5, EU wave #3, APAC wave #2)
- [ ] Create canary traffic plan and synthetic recipes (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Set up p99 smoke tests on rollout day + 72h
- [ ] Add cost-alert for GPU-hour spend spike > 22% week-over-week
- [ ] Document fallback model variants and tagging in model-catalog repo

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Reserve fraction: should we increase burst reserve to 25% for APAC initial waves? (tradeoff: cost vs p99 risk)
- Autoscaler policy: do we want cold-start buffer of 4 additional GPUs per AZ or rely on burst reserve?
- Billing: how to reflect cross-region routing cost to tenants for overflow traffic?

Notes-to-self / rough TODOs:
- Add small script to parse EV metrics and compute region drift weekly (Ravi)
- Run a focused DRILL with SRE team for EU network degradation scenario (Sofia)
- Push a short RFC for per-tenant soft caps (Evan)

References & links:
- Infra playbook (prototype): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/latency-playbooks
- Ticket: JIRA-INF-3245 (APAC vendor validation), JIRA-INF-3301 (Autoscaler policy rev)

End of draft — this doc is intentionally conversational and tactical. Will convert to a more formal runbook once Phase 1 results come in.
